title: Confirmation Resolution Broadcast
description: Payload of the confirm:resolved envelope. The server broadcasts this to every client in the session as soon as a pending destructive-operation confirmation stops being pending — because one client answered it, or because the 120-second window closed server-side. The client that answered already knows and ignores it; the other client dismisses its prompt rather than leaving it stranded (Requirement 13.5). The requestId correlating this to the original confirm:request rides on the envelope as well; it is repeated here so a payload handed to the Confirmation_Coordinator on its own is still self-describing.

requestId.description: Correlation identifier of the confirm:request this resolves. Matches the requestId the answering client echoed on its confirm:approve or confirm:reject.

decision.description: How the confirmation ended. approved and rejected come from a producer answering on one of their clients; expired means the server's 120-second window closed with no answer.

answeringClient.description: Which of the producer's clients answered, so the other one can say so rather than just dismissing the prompt. Absent when the decision is expired, because nothing answered.

$comment: answeringClient is tied to decision rather than left plainly optional so the two cannot come apart: an approved resolution that does not say who approved leaves the other client unable to explain the dismissal, and an expired resolution naming an answering client is a contradiction. Same reasoning as the success split in tool-result-partial.schema.json.
